  WHY: With `ORCH_FINAL_MERGE_REQUIRED_CHECKS=""`, auto-merge can proceed while CI is queued; severity differed (BLOCKER vs MAJOR), so the highest severity is used.

  WHY: The fixture run is counted as pending and the test can wait or fail its assertion; severity differed (BLOCKER vs MAJOR), so the highest severity is used.
- scripts/ci_budget_watch.py:38 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The watcher applies the `ai:ci-budget` label, but the label is absent from `.github/ai/label_contract.v1.json`.
  WHY: Contract-driven label synchronization does not provision it, so issue creation with that label fails and the watcher leaves no tracking issue.
- tests/test_ci_wires_every_test_file.py:28-41 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: `_is_wired` treats any occurrence of a test path in workflow YAML as proof that CI runs the test.
  WHY: A path left only in a comment or other non-executable text can make an unwired test pass the wiring guard; severity differed (NIT vs MAJOR), so the highest severity is used.
- scripts/ci_budget_watch.py:176-190 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: Marker deduplication uses a non-atomic list-then-create sequence, allowing overlapping runs to create duplicate issues for the same finding.
  WHY: Concurrent runs can both observe no existing marker before either creates its issue.
